title: Interruption; old drummer Cottrell and the Creole band
summary: After a visitor interrupts, asked about old drummers he remembers Cottrell, who played with Peter Bocage's Creole orchestra and went to New York.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: That's all it was. Come in. Good evening.

Good evening. Go back there and answer the moister. I was going to ask, we have a couple more minutes here before we finish up. Yeah, yeah. If there's any of the old time drummers you can remember, that you were, when you were a boy or just younger, that influenced you or that you liked in particular, I say for instance, old man Cottrell or some of those.
Old man Cottrell, yeah. Never knew of them. I knew him, yeah. He was a drummer. He was. Oh, yeah. He was good. But he used to play with Peter Buckeye now. Yeah. The Creole Cernet.

Oh, they made a big hit by there. They played in New York. And they made a big hit up there. They had records out. You don't have any records? Yeah, they came back here. They had all the pictures years back in Maison Blanche. They had the lyrics during that time. We told it. They had the lyrics during that time. And they played that for a week. That's a lyric, you know, on the stage. For people to see them. Yeah, they had Peter. And he had three brothers there playing. Peter Boccage, Henry Boccage. He's playing tuba. And Charlie. And Charlie was playing ghetto. And they had a fellow playing piano. He did. Steve Lewis. Steve Lewis, that's right. Yeah, he had a contract.
